full_judgment: 27. Let me now see whether the Deputy Commissioner was authorised under the law to transfer entire suit land showing different quantum of lands in the respective share to defendant Nos. 1 to 8. The decision of the then Dhaka High Court in the said case relied on by the Deputy Commissioner was on the interpretation of the provision of section 20(2) (b) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 wherein there was no definition of the family. Accordingly, it was held that wife could retain khas land within the limit separately from her husband. It may be mentioned that the Deputy Commissioner by order dated 8-4-70 before coming into operation of President's Order 98 of 1972 held that wife could retain land separately from her husband relying on the said decision. So, the said order lost its force after coming into operation of President's Order 98 of 1972. In view of the definition of family in article 2(b) of President's Order 98 of 1972 already noticed the said decision has/had no manner of application at the time of execution of the said deed of transfer in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 to 8 by the Deputy Commissioner. It is also true that a minor can own land but the question is whether he could retain land in excess of the limit as a member of a family. We have already found that defendant No. 2 Kazi Badiuzzaman was a member of the same family with his father and mother and after death of his father with his mother and other heirs of his father.
